publishedWorkflow.name: Publish application

jobs.verify: success (npm ci, npm test, build, local published-asset verification)
jobs.verify-published: success (deployed commit/runtime verification; verified release tag)

publishedWorkflow.interpretation: This establishes successful CI and publication at cf1e165. No historical test count is treated as a current requirement. For each row, the named implementation and test paths are present in the published commit tree. This does not claim that server-side MCP handlers execute inside the static Pages application.

items.acceptance: Semantic MCP edit batches work with the analysis workflow; partial/invalid batches and stale revisions are rejected atomically, without changing the saved input or existing output, while preserving compatible saved data.

proof.detail: Includes editing a saved input and subsequently analyzing the resulting file.

items.reason: Atomicity, stale-revision refusal, original-file preservation and the edit-to-analysis path have dedicated tests; all were included in the successful main npm test run. Separate actual public HTTPS pairing is tracked by PUBLICHTTPS1 and is not part of this item's acceptance.

items.acceptance: Real MCP/WASM fatigue and fracture results, simultaneous retention, paging and refusals; real local Chrome connector results match the GUI evaluation display, with invalid/stale/missing-toughness requests rejected. The connector's same-revision replacement and omitted-option defaults are accepted behavior; public HTTPS is separate.

proof.detail: Local Chrome/stdio MCP; fatigue life and damage, fracture reference, display agreement, pagination, stale revision and simultaneous assessments.
Fresh-revision missing-toughness refusal, same-revision replacement, option defaults and stale revision.

items.reason: The corrected real-Chrome evidence covers the acceptance after the earlier partial evidence; source and MCP tests are in the published commit and the publish workflow passed. HTTPS pairing, other browsers, mixed-mode/residual-stress and general physical validation remain separate/unclaimed.

items.acceptance: Common jobs expose GUI-origin work from all six structural, thermal, acoustic, channel-flow, internal-domain and exterior-domain routes; observable failures and bounded GUI history coexist with API jobs. Worker/MCP/API regression covers retention and completion behavior.

proof.detail: Real local Chrome and stdio connector: all six routes, observable failed job, GUI-only eight-entry retention, settled/releasable job states.

items.reason: The recorded real-local-browser route evidence and the job/MCP tests cover the stated scope; the deployed build and published verification passed. Disconnect continuity and intermediate field retention are covered by tests, not claimed as re-exercised in the browser run. HTTPS pairing is tracked separately.

items.acceptance: Real MCP application checks catalog revision, explicit assumptions/applicability and experimental selection; failed/stale batches are atomic. Local GUI verifies required scope, JP/EN presentation and saved/shared material equality.

proof.detail: Spawns the actual studio-mcp stdio process; checks the advertised allowlist, saved result, stale revision, atomic refusal and preservation.

items.reason: The acceptance's real MCP and local GUI requirements have dedicated evidence and tests; the code is in the successfully published build. There is no separate live interaction with the public URL for this specific GUI action, but public-HTTPS pairing is not an outstanding requirement for this item.

items.acceptance: Recompute and compare saved measurement evidence against archived result fields through the API, read-only real MCP and live semantic adapter; preserve both archives and distinguish consistency from physical accuracy.

proof.detail: Actual spawned stdio MCP; verifies replay match, tamper refusals and unchanged source archives.
Real stdio MCP and Node-hosted live adapter reproduce one saved WASM temperature field/history measurement; physicalAccuracyVerified=false.

items.reason: The saved-case replay, unchanged archives and read-only MCP requirements are verified. A new solve, real browser exercise and independent physical accuracy claim are expressly outside the accepted scope; no public HTTPS dependency is imposed.

items.acceptance: Preview changes non-destructively while a job is running; keep the input revision unchanged, then commit only the exact reviewed candidate after settlement and allow the next solve. Preserve explicit legacy/incomplete-preflight labels.

proof.detail: Real local browser/Worker evidence: 100 N solve stays running across 150 N preview; input unchanged; reviewed candidate applied after completion; next solve succeeds.
Recorded full test run before final clean CI; final source paths are included in the published commit.

items.reason: Actual local browser evidence meets the running-preview and post-settlement apply criteria, while dedicated tests cover exact revision binding and refusal. The later published CI passed on the final committed source. General physical accuracy, full P1-P3 and V8 root-cause resolution remain explicitly out of scope.

items.acceptance: Large fake-Gmsh arrays preserve tag/connectivity/quality order within an explicit higher limit and refuse over-limit arrays before unsafe spread; actual GUI size 0.6 changes from stack overflow to the existing element-limit refusal without changing the default limit.

proof.detail: Real GUI same-size check returns the existing mesh element limit error instead of stack overflow; evidence explicitly notes the first complete job archive was not captured.

items.reason: The four targeted tests and real GUI failure-mode comparison establish the narrow accepted behavior, and final main CI/build/deploy passed. The missing first-attempt full job archive, unchanged 30,000 default and unexpanded supported scale are documented limitations, not unmet acceptance criteria.

items.acceptance: Isolated single-file browser MCP starts with existing Node 24, exposes three scoped tools and validates contracts, credentials, expiry, disconnect and EOF cleanup. Bundled Node/restart recovery and public HTTPS pairing are distinct scopes.

proof.detail: Isolated local single-file startup, three tools and scoped authentication/lifecycle checks; synthetic local peer, not public HTTPS.
Actual public single-file download with manifest revision/bytes/SHA256, isolated startup/tool discovery and EOF; no browser pairing.

deployedInclusion.note: The cf1e165 publish run passed build and published asset verification; the public-download proof itself is at 0e53638 and must not be misrepresented as a cf1e165 pairing test.

items.reason: The defined single-file local connector and lifecycle acceptance is covered by dedicated tests and a prior actual public artifact download; current code is in the successfully republished source. Public HTTPS pairing remains a separate PUBLICHTTPS1 gate and is not used to hold this local connector scope.

items.acceptance: Bounded node/element connectivity pages reconstruct the same intermediate mesh and agree with saved measurements; asynchronous termination, late response, cancel/drain and field-request suppression preserve final results in real Workers.

proof.detail: Real Worker lifecycle and bounded connectivity evidence; explicitly does not claim restart recovery, full P3, peak heap bounds or public HTTPS.

items.reason: This narrow lifecycle slice meets its written acceptance and is included in the successful published build. Restart recovery and the broader P3 milestone remain unfinished and must stay separate; they do not negate this bounded slice.

items.acceptance: Reconstruct and verify retained successful job A while current input B remains unchanged; enforce refusal, expiry, disconnect/release and exact byte count/SHA/chunking using Worker-derived JSON output. Saved-case comparisons and engine/WASM identity are separate requirements.

proof.detail: Evidence states Worker module output is retained through analysis-client in Node and explicitly distinguishes this from actual browser UI testing; local full runs failed, later clean published CI is the final suite proof.

items.reason: The browser session test keeps input B unchanged while round-tripping immutable job A; the transfer and lifecycle tests cover limits and refusals, and Worker output is exercised through analysis-client in Node. The final clean main CI passed after the locally failed runs. No dedicated actual-browser transfer run is recorded, but it is not an acceptance requirement. Saved-case comparison and engine identity remain separate.
